businessModel: Free download; Standard plan $19.90/mo unlocks Neon's own AI agents
paidNote: Free plan: full browser + connect your own agents via MCP/CLI. Standard $19.90/mo: Neon Chat, Do, Make, deep research, Skills.
updateCadence: Tracks Chromium; Opera ships shared security updates
summary: Separate Opera product launched Sep 30, 2025. Free since Aug 2026 (bring your own agent via MCP/CLI); $19.90/mo Standard adds Neon Do (acts on sites), Make (builds things) and deep research. Windows and macOS only.
bestFor: Developers connecting Claude/ChatGPT agents to a real browser
People who want an ad blocker and VPN with an AI browser
Users happy to pay for cloud agents
notFor: People expecting free built-in AI chat
Those who need guaranteed MV2 extensions

pros.title: Free plan
pros.detail: Full browser at no cost since Aug 2026; works with your own agents via MCP and Opera Browser CLI.

pros.title: Built-in blocker and VPN
pros.detail: Opera's ad blocker and free VPN are included in the free plan.

pros.title: Agent variety
pros.detail: Do acts on websites; Make builds sites/tools/reports in cloud agents.

pros.title: MCP server and CLI
pros.detail: CLI needs no account and includes token compression for agent browsing.

pros.title: Established vendor
pros.detail: Opera has decades of browser shipping and shared Chromium security updates.

cons.title: AI behind $19.90/mo
cons.detail: Neon Chat, Do, Make and deep research need the Standard plan.

cons.title: Desktop only
cons.detail: Windows and macOS; no Linux or mobile apps.

cons.title: Mixed performance reviews
cons.detail: Reviewers called Do slow and the price a tough sell against free rivals.

cons.title: Confusing positioning
cons.detail: Old concept-Neon reviews contradict the 2025 product on extensions and updates.

faq.a: The browser is free since Aug 2026; Neon's own AI features need the $19.90/mo Standard plan.

switching.note: Opera import tools; extension import unverified.

jsSpeed: Blink/V8 engine, Chrome-class JS speed; no vendor benchmark
pageLoad: Chromium rendering; AI sidebar adds overhead
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and preloading
startup: Chromium cold start, heavier than plain Chrome
memory: Chromium multi-process plus AI layer; RAM-heavy
cpu: Chromium-class; agent tasks add background load
lowEnd: Needs modern hardware; AI features add load
installSize: Full Chromium bundle, a few hundred MB
privacyDefaults: Blocker and VPN but cloud agents process page data
blocking: Built-in Opera ad blocker in free plan
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox and site isolation; agent injection risk
patchSpeed: Follows Chromium stable; lag not independently measured
telemetry: Vendor telemetry; prompts processed in cloud
behaviourCustom: Few shortcut or per-site options documented
tabManagement: Tasks and Cards organise work per project
searchFreedom: Default search changeable; AI prompt flow is the focus
productivity: Chat, Do, Make and deep research on Standard
translation: AI-driven page translation; no dedicated engine
extras: Free VPN, ad blocker, MCP server and CLI
extensions: Chrome extensions reportedly work; sources conflict
passwords: Basic built-in manager or Chromium defaults
accessibility: Chromium accessibility stack, unverified for AI layer
longevity: Opera backing, but Neon repositioned within a year
ai: Strong agents on paid plan; free plan is BYO-agent
beginnerFriendly: Plan split and agent concepts confuse newcomers
